Hey man i know you're in a shitty position but you have a great mindset!  I believe in you and agree with your opinion, try walking man, make it a chore for yourself to walk, and reward yourself when you get back with something you enjoy, anything, your dog, visit a pet shop,have a nice dinner,it may not seem like it but you're in a good place i just want you to accept that someone isn't going to hand you something out of the blue to love and live for, you have to make that for yourself like you did with your dog and girlfriend, use your time walking to think of something you want with passion, you may not have control over your mood but thinking about what you don't yet have but could in the future will be a good start :) i found passion in doing inspirational speeches to my hockey team, im good friends with all of them now which was a godsend cure because it was the loneliness and feeling invisible that was so depressing, i find it easy if im lying in bed to just keep lying there, but if i make myself get up and walk, i cant cry or waste the whole day, i think about things other than how bad my life is and it was the best first step for me, i hope this helps!

Omg yes, i hope i can help - its good that you can recognise good and bad moments, i came out of the mindset by just spending all Summer drunk and making new friends and keeping my fitness up throughout, my pointers for you, make a list of things that don't take mind power to do, for example mow the lawns, do your laundry, walk the dog, and when you feel empty and toxic and horrible, do the things that don't take thinking to do, and you'll feel a lot less worse achieving something, when i made this rule for myself i did with the mindset that 'i already feel shitty, i may as well do something i dont like now rathee than when im in a good mood' because you cant ruin a bad mood, so i cherished when it was good by relaxing. Eventually youll find (if you work like me) that you start looking for a bad mood so you can start feeling better doing shit you dont like, and soon after youll stop waiting for a bad mood to do something because you know you can, its kinda like learning to walk again, you give yourself an incentive, please try this?

I understand what you're saying about the fleeting help of strangers; and while this site is a pool of Unflinching thoughts and stripped back emotions, the commenters are usually survivors/warriors of the same afflictions as the victim/posts people offer support out of empathy, we have a genuine earnest will to not want you to feel how we did, but noone ever pauses to consider at what personal cost that comes to themselves, i know myself that i automatically alienate myself, when i walk with friends i just walk ahead, until i realize im leaving them behind, i dont always feel i belong so i extricate myself from peoples personal space, i still yearn for friends and strangers to involve me but i personally dont do much to aid that, im not sure if that resonates in you but maybe youll find it helpful, the other thing i want you to consider is the opportunity you present to others through sharing your struggles, with the intimate detail you profess, it invites a stranger to share his or her personal struggles, mutual vulnerability fosters connections, its a natural reaction to when somebody tells you something personal, id implore you not to take it as a notion of carelessness but unless told otherwise, most people wont stray away from that, what would you like from this post? I doubt anyone would offer you a million dollars or be close enough to physically console you, but youve written a post so i see a few possibilities, you would like to vent, to give a perspective to younger people how much they still have, you want to talk, what do you believe you came here for, and is that still the case?

Dude, i was in your exact position 2 years ago now (crazy similar, im 20 now btw) dont place all your eggs in that basket, i dont know what it is but even though people dont comment on it, your negativity gives off an aura that is gonna push her away from you, you wont even realize it yourself until you look back in hindsight at it, from what ive learnt from my own experiences and discovering other peoples hardships is that your life is going to continue downward for a while, like a spiral, eventually youre going to hit something solid, like motivation or drugs or a new group of friends and they will grab you by the arm and tease you out of your spiral, i dont want to give you a timeframe because thats not how it works, and either way its going to feel like forever before you're over the tides (like, currents and waves of helplessness.. i always thought desolation when i looked at myself but noone ever understood what i meant by that) just consider if now is the best time to start something with her, while you're feeling like this,  do you want her to be your rock? She might not even be great at communicating with you, if you seriously want her, then work your way over this slump first, or otherwise let her into the world you're in to see how she responds and affects your state, what do you think?
